summary: This note describes a multi-pitch analysis project that estimates the fundamental frequencies (F0s) of polyphonic audio and organizes them by source. It defines three levels of the task per MIREX (multi-pitch estimation, note tracking, and multi-pitch estimation with streaming) and describes a two-stage system that reaches the hardest level. Stage 1 uses a maximum likelihood model with iterative greedy search and reports comparisons against Klapuri'ISMIR06 and Pertusa'ICASSP08 on the Bach10 dataset; Stage 2 frames streaming as constrained clustering using timbral features and a novel constrained clustering algorithm.
one_line: A two-stage system for multi-pitch estimation and streaming of polyphonic audio, using maximum likelihood estimation and constrained clustering.
key_facts: Multi-pitch analysis estimates the frequency and number of pitches at each time frame in polyphonic audio and organizes them by source.
MIREX, an annual evaluation campaign for Music Information Retrieval algorithms, describes multi-pitch analysis at three levels.
Level 1 (easiest) is Multi-pitch Estimation, which estimates pitch values of all concurrent sources at each time frame without determining their sources.
Level 3 (hardest) is Multi-pitch Estimation and Streaming, which is also called timbre tracking.
The Stage 1 likelihood model is defined on both spectral peaks and non-peak regions, where non-peak regions are frequencies further than a musical quarter tone from all observed peaks.
Stage 1 parameters are learned from thousands of randomly-mixed block chords with different polyphony.
The polyphony estimation histogram in Figure 4 uses 1000 musical chords of each polyphony generated from the Iowa instrument note sample data set.
Each box in the Figure 3 comparison represents 330 data points, with each point corresponding to 1 second of audio on the Bach10 dataset.
The Stage 2 streaming approach uses harmonic structure as the timbral feature for musical instruments, following the authors' earlier paper DuanEtal'08.
For speech talkers, the authors explore MFCC and Uniform Discrete Cepstrum (UDC) features, where UDC is newly proposed and needs no source separation.
The Stage 2 must-link constraint assigns pitches that are close in both time and frequency to the same cluster.
The Stage 2 cannot-link constraint prevents (nearly) simultaneous pitches from being assigned to the same cluster.
The proposed constrained clustering algorithm strictly decreases the timbral objective function while the set of satisfied constraints non-strictly expands.
The example piece "Ach Gott und Herr" is a four-part J.S. Bach chorale played by violin, clarinet, saxophone and bassoon.
